$comment: Reviewer registry for this repository, a port of dotfiles/harness/review-attestation.json
through the ts-bridge adaptation (ts-bridge #311), trimmed to the reviewers that measurably
act here. The SSOT of the SHAPE stays in dotfiles; kubelab, hive, web and ts-bridge each
carry their own copy.
Why the port was needed: this file did not exist, so `dotf pr triage-queue` could not answer
at all: `read reviewer registry: open harness/review-attestation.json: no such file or
directory`. Its exit status is 1 both when triage is pending AND when the question cannot be
computed, precisely so an unanswerable queue is never mistaken for a clear one. A check that
reports the same thing every time it runs stops being read, which is how a gate degrades
into noise. Ported 2026-09-06.
review_markers ARE MEASURED HERE, NOT COPIED. Measured 2026-09-06 over every non-bot PR
this repository has (#4, #5, #44, #53), plus the dependabot and release-please PRs
(#41-#43, #45-#48, #52, #54, #55), reading the issue comments and the formal reviews:
## Walkthrough                -> #44 #53   (a review ran; this is the attesting marker,
posted inside CodeRabbit's summarize comment)
## Review limit reached       -> #44 #53   (the re-review after a later push hit the
free OSS quota; each also carries
'rate limited by coderabbit.ai' twice)
## Review skipped             -> none
'No actionable comments...'   -> none (the dotfiles clean-run marker never appears here)
'Actionable comments posted'  -> #44 #53, in the formal REVIEW body, not in a comment
(no CodeRabbit output)        -> #4 #5 (predate the CodeRabbit install), every
dependabot PR and the release PR #52
Two things this measurement shows that the sibling ports do not: (1) CodeRabbit DOES publish
a check-run in this repository, and it reports `pass` with the summary 'Review rate limited'
when it declined (#53), so a green CodeRabbit check is not evidence a review happened; (2) a
single PR can carry BOTH a walkthrough and a later limit notice, so the review marker attests
the first review and the declined marker says a re-review of the newest push did not run.
Note the asymmetry that survives this: a CodeRabbit run that files ONLY a formal review with no
walkthrough comment still reads as 'no reviewer output yet'. That is a property of the tool,
which scans comments, and it is why pr-stewardship still asks a human to read the diff.

reviewers.why: ADVISORY, same disposition as the dotfiles, kubelab and ts-bridge registries: its REVIEW attests, its DECLINE does not refuse. CodeRabbit's quota is a third party's billing state rather than a property of the change. Measured here 2026-09-06: both human PRs that had CodeRabbit at all (#44, #53) drew 'Review limit reached' on their re-review, so a decline that REFUSED would make the gate red on every multi-push PR and teach everyone to ignore it. An advisory decline yields `pending`, the honest answer: a reviewer that could not run is not a reviewer that refused. LOGINS MATCH WITH TRAILING '[bot]' STRIPPED AND CASE FOLDED, because the two GitHub APIs disagree: REST reports coderabbitai[bot], GraphQL reports coderabbitai. The dotfiles 'no complaints' review marker is deliberately NOT reused; see the $comment on review_markers. '## Review skipped' is kept although unobserved here: it is the vendor's own string for 'nothing reviewable' and a marker that never matches costs nothing, while a missing one would misread a skip as 'no output yet'.

PR-Agent (see .github/workflows/pr-agent.yml) runs under GITHUB_TOKEN and publishes through the COMMENTS api, so its reviews never enter reviews[] and a classifier that looked only at reviews would read every PR-Agent-reviewed PR as unattested. The marker is the `review` command's own heading. `## PR Code Suggestions` is deliberately NOT here: suggestions are not a review, which is also why auto_improve is off on the automatic path. MARKER PROVENANCE: verified in the sibling ports before being declared here (kubelab has 215 PR comments carrying '## PR Reviewer Guide' posted by github-actions[bot], dotfiles 172, per ts-bridge #315). It has NEVER been observed in garsync, because this workflow has not run here and the NAN_API_KEY secret it needs is not set yet (Actions secrets on 2026-09-06: BITACORA_PAT only). Until the owner runs `dotf secrets sync ci --repo mlorentedev/garsync` and a pr-agent run publishes the Guide, this entry is a declaration of intent, not of an actor. github-actions[bot] also authors the release-please PRs here (#52), which is why the release exemption below is keyed on diff signature and not on this login.

triage.why: The heading the pr-review-triage skill records its dispositions under, matched at line start. Declared once here and read back by `dotf pr triage-queue`, so the writer and the reader are not a two-file agreement nobody checks. Already in use here before the registry existed: #44 and #53 both carry it. A disposition that lives only in a chat message evaporates, and the Definition of Done's Review item would then rest on a claim nobody can re-read. It is posted even when there was nothing to dispose of: 'CI green, no review findings' is a disposition, and leaving it unwritten is indistinguishable from nobody having looked.

escape.label: merged-unreviewed
escape.why: Both are required, never one. Proceeding on an unreviewed PR is allowed; proceeding SILENTLY is not. The label plus the section is what forces the disclosure into the durable record instead of a chat message.

signatures.name: release-please
signatures.why: Measured on #52 (v0.2.0): exactly these four paths, because release-please bumps the Python package version in pyproject.toml and src/garsync/__init__.py in addition to the manifest and changelog (release.yml, release-type python). Matched by DIFF SIGNATURE with set equality, never by author or branch. release-please runs under GITHUB_TOKEN here so its PRs are authored by github-actions[bot], the same login PR-Agent posts under; an author rule would therefore be ambiguous, and a branch rule would let any branch named release-please--* walk past the gate. The moment such a PR touches one more file the exemption stops applying, and it stops applying just as surely if one declared file is not touched. This is not 'small PRs need no review': a release commit mechanically restates commits that were each reviewed when they landed, and reporting `declined` on it says something false.
